identityClasses.rule: Current brand copy, canonical host, contact, social metadata, active docs, and current visual assets change only in the approved phase.
Old host, routes, API compatibility, repository redirects, and email forwarding remain for the declared window.
Schema names, cookie and local-storage keys, API schema versions, database functions and settings, and release IDs do not change in the brand cutover.
Frozen release bytes, checksums, deposited citations, signed review packets, archived screenshots, filenames, and published labels are never rewritten.
Obsolete plans and mockups may retain the historical name with context; cosmetic rewriting is not a release requirement.

surfaces.renameMode: Update from one approved identity contract.
surfaces.keepMode: No change except approved risk controls.

surfaces.renameMode: Switch one canonical origin after new-host verification; old host preserves path and query.
surfaces.rollback: Restore prior SITE_URL and disable new-host indexing.

surfaces.renameMode: Repository may change after redirect tests; package and workflow identifiers stay stable through first cutover.
surfaces.rollback: Restore repository/profile pointers; internal identifiers are unchanged.

surfaces.renameMode: Keep routes, headers and frozen filenames compatible; preserve the retired embed 410 with updated successor links; future artifacts may adopt the successor slug.
surfaces.rollback: Old host and stable paths remain served.
No database or client-state migration is required.

surfaces.renameMode: Keep deposited and frozen records byte-identical; apply successor identity only to new versions with backward links.
Provision and verify successor endpoints first; retain old mail and callbacks through compatibility.
surfaces.keepMode: No change; complete existing delivery tests.
surfaces.rollback: Restore old primary endpoints; forwarding and old callbacks remain available.

surfaces.renameMode: Use an isolated preview, then staged DNS/status/monitor changes with owner authority.
surfaces.keepMode: No change; finish existing platform checks.
surfaces.rollback: Restore prior deployment/domain assignment and status links.

surfaces.renameMode: Reserve first, coordinate updates, request recrawl, retain former-handle pointers.
surfaces.keepMode: Verify ownership and recovery controls only.
surfaces.rollback: Restore display identity and canonical host while retaining successor reservation.

surfaces.renameMode: Introduce approved assets through the design system and reconcile every legal/policy surface.
surfaces.keepMode: No speculative redesign or copy change.
surfaces.rollback: Restore prior tokens/assets/policy identity; historical assets remain untouched.
